title: A $0.15 Model Tied Opus 5.5
caption:
A $0.15-a-task model matched Opus 5.5 on Vercel's Next.js agent evals, once someone handed it the docs.

Same model, same prompt, same 31 tasks. The only difference is an AGENTS.md pointing at the docs bundled inside the next package. GLM 5.2 went from 25 of 31 to 30 of 31. Opus 5.5, GPT 6 Sol and Fable 5.1 gained nothing from that file — they were already at 30.

I've been paying for the expensive model to paper over the fact that I never wrote an AGENTS.md. Embarrassing thing to learn from a leaderboard.

Which model are you on?

slides.headline:
A $0.15 Model
Tied Opus 5.5
slides.sub: On Vercel's Next.js agent evals, GLM 5.2 went from 25 of 31 tasks to 30 of 31 — matching Opus 5.5 — once the sandbox got one extra file. Last run 25 September 2026.

slides.title: One Extra File
slides.sub: Both runs use the same model, the same prompt and the same 31 tasks. One drops in an AGENTS.md telling the agent to read the docs bundled at node_modules/next/dist/docs. That is the whole difference.

slides.title: Who The Docs Fixed
items: GLM 5.2 — 25 of 31, then 30 of 31. $0.152 a task.
Claude Sonnet 5 — 25 of 31, then 30 of 31. $0.386 a task.
Kimi K3 — 26 of 31, then 30 of 31. $0.281 a task.
Gemini 3.8 Flash — 28 of 31, then 30 of 31. $0.605 a task.
GPT 6 Astra — 28 of 31, then 30 of 31. $0.891 a task.

slides.title: The Top Four Gained Nothing
items: Claude Opus 5.5 — 30 of 31 either way. $0.234 a task.
GPT 6 Sol — 30 of 31 either way. $0.244 a task.
Claude Fable 5.1 — 30 of 31 either way. $0.722 a task.
Grok 4.7 — 29 of 31 either way. $0.109 a task.

slides.headline:
Stale Training
Data
slides.sub: Vercel says the point of the suite is to "find places where agents get Next.js wrong because their training data is stale, then fix it by shipping better docs in the next package itself." Docs don't raise a model's ceiling. They stop a cheaper one guessing.

slides.title: What This Doesn't Say
items: Scores are pass@4 — a task counts if any of four attempts works.
31 Next.js tasks. Nothing here about your stack.
Average list cost per task, not what a seat costs you.
